title: Add lightweight RAG test scenarios and instrumentation guide
author: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Motivation: Provide a compact, opinionated developer guide and set of quickstart scenarios for testing RAG/agent integrations with instrumentation hooks. Many users ask how to validate correctness and regressions for tool-calling flows and retrieval fallbacks without running full e2e infra. This PR adds a focused docs guide + runnable artifacts (devcontainer + CI smoke tests + small synthetic dataset) so teams can reproduce and iterate locally.

What this PR contains (single continuous description): Updated docs under /docs/rag/testing to introduce three canonical test scenarios (happy-path retrieval, retrieval empty/fallback, and tool-invocation error handling) plus a lightweight telemetry pattern to assert behavioral signals. The guide includes: 1) a curated prompt corpus and expected-checks.json for deterministic checks; 2) a devcontainer recipe with a small local vectorstore Docker sleep-image and a runner script (scripts/rag-smoke-runner.sh) that exercises the scenarios end-to-end; 3) a set of telemetry probes (examples/telemetry-probes.md) that maps Redwood Console metrics and spans to test assertions; 4) two CI jobs (ci/rag-smoke.yml, ci/rag-lint.yml) that run the runner and check traces/metrics exported to a local OTLP collector stub.

Commits (high-level): - 12fd2e3 Add guide and scenario descriptions - 8b4a9f1 Add devcontainer and runner script with docker-compose stub - c1a7e2b Add expected-checks.json and prompt corpus (10 prompts) - e3f4b88 Add CI smoke job and OTLP stub - 9c0b5d2 Docs polishing and review feedback fixes

Files changed (high level): - docs/rag/testing/index.md (new) - docs/rag/testing/scenarios.md (new) - examples/telemetry-probes.md (new) - devcontainer/devcontainer.json (modified) - scripts/rag-smoke-runner.sh (new) - ci/rag-smoke.yml (new) - ci/otlp-stub/docker-compose.yml (new)

Checklist / acceptance criteria: - [x] Guide explains what to instrument (request latencies, kv-cache hit ratios, model-fallback metrics, tool-call success/failure) - [x] Runner reproduces scenarios locally in <2 minutes on a developer laptop (with Docker) - [x] CI job runs headless and posts simple pass/fail artifact + trace snapshot - [x] Examples map Console metric names to assertions so teams can wire alerts - [x] No prod secrets required; uses local stubbed services only

Review conversation summary (condensed into single string): Luca: "Nice focused scope — can we add an explicit section on nondeterministic output handling so teams understand fuzzy matching?" Maya: "Good call — added expected-checks.json and guidance on soft matching thresholds; included a helper assert_soft_match() in the runner." Priya: "CI job should not rely on external network — confirm OTLP collector is entirely local." Maya: "Confirmed; otlp-stub runs in the CI container compose and CI job blocks until it receives spans." Noah: "Docs should recommend metric cardinality controls for telemetry probes." Maya: "Added a short note about sampling and cardinality under telemetry-probes.md."

CI summary: Initial pipelines had a lint warning (doc link formatting) which was fixed; first smoke run failed due to a timing race when the OTLP stub accepted traces late — added a simple retry with backoff in rag-smoke-runner.sh; subsequent CI run passed. The PR's ci_status is pass and the smoke artifacts (trace snapshots and expected-checks diff) were attached to the job.

Testing notes and reproducibility: To run locally, clone repo, open devcontainer or run ./scripts/rag-smoke-runner.sh --local. The runner spins up a tiny SQLite-backed vectorstore, an OTLP stub that writes spans to /tmp/rag-traces.json, and posts a single inference request to the local redwood dev API shim (included in scripts) that simulates model variants. The expected-checks.json contains simple predicates (exact, regex, soft_similarity) against the generated response and telemetry exports. The guide recommends thresholds for soft_similarity and describes how to map a failure to Console dashboards/alerts.

Backward compatibility and release notes: non-breaking docs-only change. Release note: "Added developer quickstart: RAG testing & telemetry guide — includes runnable smoke harness, sample prompt corpus, and CI job to validate retrieval + tool-calling flows."

Merge outcome: Squashed and merged into main after approvals from Luca and Priya. No outstanding action items.

Why this is different from existing quickstarts: Most examples focus on building RAG apps; this PR emphasizes reproducible regression tests and telemetry-driven assertions that teams can adopt quickly without full infra. It's intentionally compact and designed as a template to be copied into product repos or platform onboarding checklists.
